output.summary: Fruit tree native to the eastern and central United States. Its deeply plated bark is distinctive, and its orange fruit is astringent when unripe but sweet when ripe; ripe fruit may be eaten raw, usually after softening, or cooked or dried.
output.edibilityNote: Ripe fruit is eaten raw, usually after softening, or cooked, dried, fermented or made into desserts, jam, molasses and candy.
